findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` method definition overrides the 4-argument version
findings.body: Two class methods named `downsize` are defined: one at line 145 taking `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and another at line 149 taking `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby, the second definition completely replaces the first. Any existing caller elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. thumbnail-generation jobs) that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` with four positional arguments will now raise an ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments) because only the 3-arg version is reachable. This silently removes the old API contract and will break any code outside this diff that still uses the old signature.

findings.title: Downsize loop does not verify success and can silently exceed configured max size
findings.body: The new loop (lines 64-70) calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` up to 5 times while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, but it never checks the boolean return value of `downsize` (which returns false on failure, e.g. ImageMagick error). If a downsize attempt fails, the loop just burns an attempt without actually shrinking the file, and after 5 failed/insufficient attempts the code proceeds to create the upload anyway, silently allowing an image larger than `max_image_size_kb` to be stored — defeating the purpose of the limit without any error being surfaced to the user or logs.

findings.title: In-place downsize uses identical path for source and destination
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` passes the same path as both `from` and `to`. For animated GIFs this dispatches to `gifsicle ... --output #{to}` with `from == to`, and for static images to ImageMagick `convert`. Overwriting the same file that is simultaneously used as input is risky (depending on tool buffering behavior) and can produce a truncated/corrupted file if the external process fails partway or does not fully buffer input before writing output, resulting in a corrupted upload being stored for the user.

findings.title: API URL download size limit hardcoded, ignoring site setting
findings.body: The download size cap for API-provided URLs was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. This removes administrator control over the maximum allowed download size for API uploads; sites configured with a smaller `max_image_size_kb` will now allow downloads up to 10MB regardless, and sites that intentionally allowed larger downloads via the setting are now capped at 10MB. This is a behavior/API contract change that isn't mentioned in the PR description and isn't configurable.

findings.title: Client-side upload size validation hardcoded, ignoring per-type site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously computed `maxSizeKB` from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, honoring separate configured limits for images vs. attachments. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` (10MB) for all upload types, so admin-configured limits (e.g. a smaller max_attachment_size_kb, or any limit different from 10MB) are no longer enforced client-side. This creates inconsistent behavior between client-side pre-validation and actual server-side limits, confusing users with incorrect error messages or allowing oversized attachments to be submitted before failing server-side.

findings.title: 413 error handler hardcodes max size instead of using the image-specific site setting
findings.body: `displayErrorForUpload` previously read `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to report the correct max size in the 413 (entity too large) error message. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024`, so the error message shown to the user may not match the actual configured (or newly auto-downsized) limit, producing a misleading error message when the real limit differs from 10MB.

findings.title: No test coverage for new automatic image downsizing behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a non-trivial feature (automatically downsizing oversized images on upload, with a retry loop and in-place file modification) but includes no new or updated tests for `UploadsController#create_upload` covering: successful downsizing under the limit, downsizing failing to converge within 5 attempts, or the interaction with `allow_animated_thumbnails`. This is a user-facing behavioral change with no verification that it works as intended.
